The shipping projection/orientation convention is right. The W4b coverage gap is real and still open, but it is a coverage gap only — neither mutation is the current behaviour, and both are genuine defects that an independent fixture detects immediately.

1. FIRST-PRINCIPLES DERIVATION (CONFIRMED by hand + numpy).

Template side: OrientationPlan.swift:178 takes basis = ACOMOrientation.detectorBasis(n); :192-194 sets x = g·e1, y = g·e2, azim = atan2(y, x). detectorBasis (OrientationResult.swift:91-95) builds e1 = normalize(n x ref), e2 = n x e1, columns (e1, e2, n) — right-handed, since e1 x e2 = n. So the template azimuth zero is e1 = matrix column 0, and positive azimuth turns e1 -> e2 right-handedly about n.
Experimental side: OrientationMatcher.swift:239-242 uses dx = x - originX, dy = y - originY, azim = atan2(dy, dx), with BraggPeak x = column, y = row (DiskDetection.swift:34 and :634-639, index i = y*px + x). So the experimental azimuth zero is detector +x = column, positive toward +y = row.
Composition: ACOMOrientation.matrix (OrientationResult.swift:99-105) returns basis * Rz with Rz columns (c,-s,0),(s,c,0),(0,0,1). If the pattern is the template rotated by theta (phi_exp = phi_tmpl + theta), then the true detector-x axis in crystal coords is E1 = e1 cos(theta) - e2 sin(theta) and E2 = e1 sin(theta) + e2 cos(theta) — exactly the columns of basis * Rz(theta). So `angle` must be the pattern's rotation relative to the template.
Sign of the correlation shift: vDSP_zvmul(..., -1) at OrientationMatcher.swift:165-168 conjugates the FIRST factor (experimental), giving corr[m] = sum_a exp[a]*tmpl[a+m], whose argmax is m = -theta. Line 313-314 negates it (bin = (N - bestBin) % N). Net: angle = +theta. Consistent.
Handedness anchor: the app's sg = g·n + (lambda/2)|g|^2 (OrientationPlan.swift:186) equals MINUS py4DSTEM's sg (~g_z - lambda|g|^2/2, k0 = [0,0,-1/lambda] at crystal_ACOM.py:716) precisely when n = -(py4DSTEM lab z); the Gaussian is even so the sign is irrelevant. Independently, py4DSTEM's lab z IS the zone axis: I verified numerically that column 2 of m1z@m2x@m3z (crystal_ACOM.py:612-712) equals orientation_vecs exactly, det = 1.0. Therefore the app's n is the beam PROPAGATION direction (downstream). For the app's matrix (col, row, n) to be a proper rotation, (column, row, downstream) must be right-handed — which is exactly the standard detector convention, confirmed from py4DSTEM's own plotting: plot_diffraction_pattern (crystal_viz.py:945, scatter ~1010, invert_yaxis :1072) puts qy on the horizontal (right) and qx on the vertical inverted (down), i.e. qx = row, qy = column, and (row, column, zone axis) right-handed puts the zone axis out of the screen with the beam going in. The two frames therefore differ by app_x = py_y, app_y = py_x, app_z = -py_z, i.e. M_app = M_py @ P with P = [[0,1,0],[1,0,0],[0,0,-1]] — a proper rotation (det +1), and byte-identical to the lab_swap the comparator derives at tools/training-dataset-campaign/parity_py4dstem.py:427.
py4DSTEM structural match: its template phi = arctan2(g[1], g[0]) (crystal_ACOM.py:800), experimental qphi = arctan2(qy, qx) (:1043), and final composition orientation_matrix @ m3z (:1547) with m3z byte-identical to the app's inPlane. py4DSTEM conjugates the REFERENCE (:868) instead of the experimental image, hence no negation there; the app conjugates the experimental image and negates. The two are the same convention by two routes.
Under either mutation the app frame would relate to py4DSTEM's by a det = -1 map, which cannot be a frame relabelling. So the mutations are wrong science, as the open item says — but they are not what ships.

2. INDEPENDENT ANALYTIC FIXTURE (CONFIRMED, I ran it). I wrote a probe that builds the "experimental" peaks itself from a right-handed basis (f1, f2, n) constructed in the probe — never calling OrientationPlan.project — and compares the matcher's exported orientation against the known truth with a symmetry-aware misorientation (24 cubic / 12 D6 operators built in the probe). harnessResults: RAN tools/acom-groundtruth/run.sh on an analytic fixture I generated (/tmp/acomprobe/gt-input.json, 6 FCC Au patterns whose peak positions come from a basis I constructed, not from project()): exit 0, ~8.7 s. Its exported orientationMatrixRowMajor vs the known truth, symmetry-reduced over the 24 proper cubic operators: 0.637, 1.286, 1.250, 1.525, 0.442, 2.815 deg. det = 1.0000 on all six. Its in-plane angles reproduced my standalone probe's byte for byte (53.44, 222.19, 348.75, 151.87, 61.87, 239.06 deg).

WHAT acom-groundtruth ACTUALLY COMPARES: nothing. It is a JSON-in/JSON-out CLI wrapping Crystal + OrientationPlan + OrientationMatcher (CPU). It has no reference, no assertions, no pass/fail, and no committed driver; it exits 0 whenever the plan and matcher initialise. It is NOT in tools/run-tests.sh:70-88. STRENGTH: because it takes peaks from JSON and never calls project() to build them, a driver that supplies analytically-derived or py4DSTEM-derived peaks DOES catch both mutations decisively (measured below). As committed — no driver, no expectations — it catches nothing.

ANALYTIC PROBE, CUBIC (FCC Au a=4.08, kMax 1.2, 200 kV, 600 templates, intensityPower 0.25, corr kernel 0.08 A^-1 — production settings from AppState.swift:5125). 18 generic zone axes x 8 in-plane angles = 144 trials. SHIPPING: median |d_phi| 1.10 deg (azimuthal bin is 2pi/128 = 2.81 deg, so the half-bin floor is 1.41 deg); mean d_phi over the near-correct population -0.027 deg (no systematic bias); 131/144 within 20 deg of truth, 0/144 near +-90 deg; misorientation vs analytic truth median 1.25 deg, p90 2.50 deg.

SAME PROBE, MUTANT A (e1<->e2 transpose at OrientationPlan.swift:192-193, applied to a /tmp copy of Core/): median |d_phi| 88.63 deg; only 36/144 within 20 deg, 43/144 near +-90 deg; misorientation median 36.72 deg, p90 57.58 deg.
SAME PROBE, MUTANT B (azim: atan2(-y, x) at OrientationPlan.swift:194): median |d_phi| 91.07 deg; 17/144 within 20 deg, 64/144 near +-90 deg; misorientation median 35.98 deg, p90 50.87 deg.

ANALYTIC PROBE, HEXAGONAL (Crystal.tungstenDisulfide, a=3.1532, c=12.323, symmetry .hexagonal, kMax 1.6, 1518 reflections, D6 operators rebuilt in the probe). 30 zone axes x 8 in-plane angles = 240 trials. SHIPPING: 240/240 within 20 deg of truth, 0 near +-90, 0 pi-flips; median |d_phi| 0.42 deg; misorientation median 0.79 deg, p90 1.89 deg, max 3.16 deg. MUTANT A: median misorientation 63.44 deg, 0/240 correct. MUTANT B: median 62.04 deg, 16/240 correct. So the non-cubic path is right too, and is equally discriminable.

py4DSTEM END-TO-END (py4DSTEM 0.14.17 in the `py4dstem` conda env; numpy 2.5 needed a float_/dtype shim applied after import). 40 random orientations; patterns from py4DSTEM's own Crystal.generate_diffraction_pattern (sigma 0.03/sqrt2 to match the app's Gaussian width, sg_max 0.1, k_max 1.2, 200 kV); qx->app y, qy->app x; fed through the SHIPPED tools/acom-groundtruth; scored as misorientation(M_app, M_py @ lab_swap) over the 24 cubic operators. SHIPPING: median 2.06 deg, p25 0.97, p75 37.78, 62% under 5 deg, mean score 0.799. MUTANT A: median 36.75 deg, 3% under 5 deg, mean score 0.811. MUTANT B: median 31.73 deg, 3% under 5 deg, mean score 0.811. NULL (no frame map, M_app vs M_py): median 35.50 deg, 0% under 5 deg. The historical claim in docs/py4dstem-pipelines.md section 10.1 (3.05 deg median, curved + power 0.25) reproduces.

FAILURE BREAKDOWN of the 15/40 py4DSTEM cases above 5 deg for the shipping code: 3 are exact 180-degree in-plane flips (misorientation drops to 1.91, 3.63, 4.07 deg after applying Rz(180) to the truth) — the documented, weakly broken pi-degeneracy; 4 have a zone-axis error above 5 deg (5.5, 12.8, 13.8, 14.2 deg) at low scores (0.52-0.87); the rest are intermediate in-plane errors consistent with the two codebases' differing structure-factor/Gaussian models plus the 2.81 deg azimuthal bin and the ~2-3 deg template bank. NONE of them is a 90-degree or mirrored answer.

SCORE IS BLIND: mean correlation score on identical py4DSTEM input was 0.799 (shipping) vs 0.811 (mutant A) vs 0.811 (mutant B). No score or reliability threshold can detect this defect class — worth recording alongside the W4b reliability blind spot already in docs/open-items.md.
acom.whatWouldSettleIt:
Nothing further is needed for the verdict — it is settled. What is still OWED is the gate, and it is now cheap because the discriminating fixtures exist and are known to work.

Concretely, three things:

1. Land the analytic fixture as a repo harness. My probes are at /tmp/acomprobe/main.swift (cubic FCC Au) and /tmp/acomprobe/hex/main.swift (hexagonal 2H-WS2), built by /tmp/acomprobe/build.sh, which is tools/acom-groundtruth/run.sh's source list with the harness main swapped. The essential property is that the "experimental" peaks are built from a right-handed basis (f1, f2, n) constructed IN THE HARNESS — never by calling OrientationPlan.project — and scored by a symmetry-aware misorientation whose operator set is also built in the harness. Suggested gate thresholds from the measurements: cubic median misorientation < 3 deg with at least 120/144 trials inside 20 deg of the true in-plane angle; hexagonal median < 2 deg with 240/240 inside 20 deg. Both mutants blow through those by an order of magnitude (36-63 deg medians), so break-the-test verification is a two-line sed on a copy of Core/, exactly as I did it.

2. Gate tools/acom-groundtruth by giving it a committed driver and expectations. The generator I used is /tmp/acomprobe/py4gen.py (py4DSTEM 0.14.17, needs the numpy-2 float_/dtype shim applied AFTER importing py4DSTEM, or a pinned numpy<2 env). Its output /tmp/acomprobe/py4-input.json plus the truth matrices /tmp/acomprobe/py4-truth.npy would let CI assert median misorientation(M_app, M_py @ lab_swap) < 5 deg without needing py4DSTEM at run time — the JSON and the truth array can be checked in as a frozen fixture. That also closes the second W4b item (the exported matrix decoupled from the reported template index), because the check is on the exported matrix against an external truth.

3. Separately, open a Gate D item for the two real weaknesses this exposed, which are NOT convention bugs: the ~9% rate of exact 180-degree in-plane flips on clean synthetic FCC Au, and the fact that the match score is identical (0.799 vs 0.811) for correct and mirrored projections, so no confidence metric can flag either. The pi-degeneracy is documented as weakly broken by Ewald curvature; what is not documented is that it still fires roughly one position in ten on noise-free patterns, which bounds how much any per-position in-plane angle can be trusted on real data.

The one honest gap in my own evidence: the py4DSTEM cross-check is cubic only, because I generated FCC Au and parity_py4dstem.py:348-360 refuses non-cubic. The non-cubic path is covered by the hexagonal analytic probe (240/240) but has no py4DSTEM anchor. Adding a hexagonal arm to the py4DSTEM generator would close that, and is straightforward since py4DSTEM's Crystal takes an arbitrary cell.

ux.summary: The app is in better UI/UX shape than a codebase this size usually is: task-scoping is genuinely implemented (14 `workspaceArea`/`analysisMode` gates in the sidebar), empty states and disabled-reason text are widespread, the disk-detection panel has a real acceptance-funnel diagnostic, the main viewer's colorbar carries true value range + units + gamma + zero mark + masked indicator, and the vocabulary is a microscopist's rather than a programmer's ("Probe radius", "Fit residual", "Fit annulus", "Flip 180°"). I found no jargon problem worth reporting and I am not padding the list with one. What is wrong falls into three groups. (1) Three defects where a wrong reading is easy and the app's own strongest signals are the thing misleading: the green "Quantitative" badge is a fallthrough default that never consults calibration and escapes into the exported PNG and its XMP; each comparison panel is independently min-max normalized with no scale shown and a hardcoded viridis, so the view built for comparing two results is the one view that cannot be compared by eye; and a saved scientific result is deleted from disk by one click of a small borderless icon with no confirmation and no undo anywhere in the app. (2) Reach and first contact: the launch screen's three cards are inert, oversized, and teach a vocabulary (Prepare/Analyze/Preserve) the app immediately abandons (Prepare/Image/Map/Reconstruct/Results); once a dataset is open, "Open with Options…" — v2's headline crop/bin feature — plus Recents and the demo become unreachable without ⌘N; every error shares one "Something went wrong" title, including the carefully-written sidecar message; there is no Help book and no Finder document types. (3) Everything that says a loaded cube is not the whole file lives in an inspector pane that defaults to closed. Separately, the Track B checklist has drifted from the build: F1.42 names a "File ▸ Open Demo" menu item that does not exist and F1.8 describes a state the app cannot enter — the same class S18's own Gate A caught in F1.36. S18 was a bounded engineering sweep (overlay collision, scroll monitor, comparison `contentVersion`, residency plumbing); it explicitly did not cover trust labelling, navigation, first-run, or error presentation, which is most of what is left.

trackb.freeFormVerdict:
WHAT FREE-FORM CATCHES THAT THE CHECKLIST WOULD NOT (the honest case FOR the proposal):

1. Unanticipated defects. The repo's own record is the strongest argument the owner has. checklist:10-15: 2026-08-06, tag day, all 30 harnesses green — ten minutes of hand-driving produced two real defects (a colormap control absent from the only workspace that needed it; a readiness row contradicting its own detail line). 2026-08-14, first clean-account run, ~15 minutes — three more, none reachable by any harness. Neither of those came from a row. A checklist can only find what someone already suspected; that is its structural ceiling, and CLAUDE.md:36-40 names it.

2. Data monoculture is a live, MEASURED problem here. The policy set is four cubes (development-process.md §8): sim_Au, Si_SiGe, Particle_1, polycrystal_2D_WS2. Two W4b findings this week came from a specimen class the others cannot express — a ~2.21-2.26× (0002) reference-shell mis-scale on a basal specimen, and reliability ranking a wrong Q scale above the right one on near-degenerate templates. Session memory carries "never calibrate a frame convention on a single-grain dataset". Varied real cubes with different scan aspect ratios, detector sizes, dtypes and multi-dataset layouts will exercise paths no fixture reaches. CONFIRMED as a pattern; the specific yield is PLAUSIBLE.

3. It is the only way to unblock TB1 sitting 3. development-process.md §9 lists "One multi-GB cube reachable locally" as a standing data-availability block with state "Largest local cube is 1.3 GB". Sitting 3 (F1.14/F1.15/F1.19/F1.22/F1.23) and Done criterion 3 are gated on data, not judgement. If the owner's own datacubes are multi-GB, driving them IS the missing resource — this is the single highest-value thing in the proposal.

4. Intermittent and stateful defects. F1.33's stale scroll monitor (checklist:255) is application-wide and hover-triggered; its own row admits "the old behaviour is intermittent by nature, so 'it works' on one attempt is not evidence". Natural app-switching over an hour provokes it better than a scripted probe.

5. Unprimed judgement. F1.37 (checklist:260) asks whether the dead band outside a letterboxed image "reads as broken". Telling the owner the band is deliberate destroys the only measurement the row wanted. Same for F1.40's wording. For this class, reading the row first makes the answer worse.

WHAT IT MISSES:

1. Absence checks. F1.3 (there is no control that exports a preview), F1.14 (the section must be GONE), F1.31 (no orange refusal). You cannot notice the absence of a thing you were not told to look for. This is not a diligence problem; it is a logic one.

2. Deliberate-failure checks. F1.23, F1.15, and Done criterion 3's "a failure made to halt honestly". Nobody sabotages their own analysis casually.

3. Constructed fixtures. F1.26's impossible sidecar, F1.42's simple-cubic-on-gold demo. These states do not occur in real work; that is why they were built.

4. Silent wrongness on data with no ground truth. This is the one that should decide it. Section C (checklist:76-82) exists because "a run that finds only the central beam still produces a number and a green step", and §C is annotated as "the whole reason Track B exists". On his OWN cubes the owner has no analytic answer to check against — that is exactly the condition under which a wrong number looks fine. F1.45 is the live instance: the app will hand him a mis-scaled Q and a reliability number that looks healthy. Free-form on unfamiliar data is strong at "is this ugly / broken / stuck" and weak at "is this WRONG", and the second is what this app's contract is about.

5. The bookkeeping, which is not clerical here. checklist:270-278 requires the date, the dataset, what was driven and every finding, in docs/open-items.md, because "findings must not live only in a chat log". A free-form session that finds nothing produces no evidence that anything was verified — it cannot tick DC2 or DC13, and it cannot be re-checked by a later reader. The repo's stated rule (CLAUDE.md:184-186) is that no claim stands that a reader cannot reproduce.

6. Evidence quality drifts without a row to score against. Three recorded instances: F1.3b was once scored PASSED because the dialog appeared while both preview panes were blank (track-b skill); it was finally closed by a five-cold-open colour census against a matched negative control, not by eye (checklist:206). F1.17 was "PARTLY PASSED ... in several screenshots" until a re-drive produced exact geometry (scroll area y188-809 vs caption y805-831, 22 of 26 points below the edge) — checklist:239. F1.27's same-file re-grant branch is STILL not scored because one screenshot cannot establish whether Change… was used or the panel was cancelled (checklist:249). Free-form output defaults to the weak form of all three.

7. The eval-only rule is at its greatest risk here. CLAUDE.md:277-279 and checklist:41-43: never modify app logic to make an acceptance step pass; a blockage is a FINDING. Driving his own science, the owner is a user, and users want the thing fixed so they can continue. This is the one discipline the proposal quietly erodes, and it should be restated explicitly rather than assumed.
trackb.recommendation:
RECOMMENDATION — reorder and add, do not substitute. Six concrete moves.

1. FREE-FORM FIRST, UNPRIMED, THEN THE ROWS — same sitting.
Budget 20-30 minutes on his own cubes BEFORE he reads any row text, then run the scripted rows. The order matters and is not stylistic: F1.37 and F1.40 are asking whether something reads as broken/as a warning, and reading the trap first is what destroys that measurement. Both halves are cheap; the sequence is free.

2. TELL HIM WHICH ROWS HIS OWN DATA IS THE ONLY KEY TO — and spend his time there.
If any of his cubes is multi-GB, ONE real rehearse → promote on it is worth more than everything else in the proposal combined: it closes Done criterion 3 (v2-release.md:210-219), which is blocked on data availability alone (development-process.md §9). Ask for that explicitly. Same for the multi-dataset-switching row (checklist:62) and the tall-narrow-scan colorbar/scale-bar row (checklist:88), which want shapes the policy set does not have.

3. WHAT HE MUST CAPTURE, so a finding is evidence and not anecdote. Six items per observation — this list is derived from the three recorded cases where a Track B observation could not be scored (F1.3b, F1.17, F1.27):
   a. THE BUILD. Confirm ⌘R from Xcode, never `open -a mac4DSTEM` (that launches the installed release; cost recorded 2026-08-19, track-b skill). Plus `git rev-parse --short HEAD` pasted once at the start of the sitting.
   b. THE DATASET, by full path, plus shape (Ry×Rx×Qy×Qx), file size and format. "One of my cubes" is unusable; F1.26 and F1.45 both turn on properties of a specific file.
   c. THE EXACT CLICK PATH to the state, in order, including anything he changed off defaults. F1.45 is unreachable at shipped defaults (ACOM refuses at ~1 peak/pattern) — a report that omits "I raised min relative intensity" is unreproducible.
   d. A FULL-WINDOW screenshot, not a crop. F1.17 could not be scored from cropped shots for two days; geometry is the evidence for every clipping and collision row.
   e. STRINGS VERBATIM, especially the status line and any error. Two specific ones: copy the whole line after "HDF5 reported:", and copy the errno — checklist:210 records that `errno = 1 'Operation not permitted'` means the sandbox while `errno = 13 'Permission denied'` means it is NOT the sandbox, and an earlier version of that row named the wrong one and would have sent the diagnosis the wrong way.
   f. EXPECTED, THEN OBSERVED, in that order, in his own words. "I thought X would happen" is the half that makes an unanticipated finding legible later; it is also the half a free-form session naturally drops.
   And one negative result per sitting: "opened N cubes, drove these workspaces, found nothing" — dated, in docs/open-items.md. A pass with no findings is a claim, and it needs the same record.

4. THREE STANDING CAUTIONS TO HAND HIM WITH THE PROPOSAL:
   - DO NOT copy his own cubes into References/training_dataset/. development-process.md §8: `tools/real-data-acceptance/run.sh` and the campaign runner both glob `*.h5` there, so every file dropped in silently joins the aggregate gate and changes what green means. Bulk data lives outside; harnesses take explicit paths.
   - DO NOT drive the app while `tools/run-tests.sh unit` is running. CLAUDE.md:124-128 records a spurious SidebarDensityMeasurementTests failure on 2026-08-31 from exactly this — two people sharing one defaults domain.
   - The eval-only rule, restated in one sentence: if the app blocks his science, that is a finding for docs/open-items.md, not a change to make it go. This is the discipline most at risk when the driver is doing real work rather than scoring rows.

5. BUY BACK THE OWNER'S TIME instead of cutting the checklist — this is what makes the reorder cost nothing. With Screen Recording + Accessibility granted (re-grant after every Claude Code update — session memory), the assistant can drive and score the presence/absence/layout/text rows itself: that is how F1.32 was scored and how F1.34's truncation was caught while all 384 tests stayed green. Candidates to move off the owner's plate now: F1.38 (visit every image surface — mechanical), F1.39 (read one label and one caption), F1.34's narrow-sidebar re-drive, F1.33(a) (provokable via ⌘-Tab), F1.30's shape assertion. Real CGEvent clicks and drags work, so drag-dependent rows are no longer owner-only (checklist:176-182). What stays owner-only: judgement calls, the clean account, and anything needing his multi-GB data.

6. TWO DOC FIXES THIS ASSESSMENT TURNED UP, worth doing regardless of the decision:
   - WRITE THE MISSING COLLEAGUE-SIDECAR ROW (call it F1.46). Done criterion 4 is the only criterion with no numbered row, no expected result and no cited control — it exists solely as prose at checklist:137-140. Under the track-b skill's own rule ("cite the control, with file:line, for every row you queue" — the rule that would have prevented F1.1 and F1.36), a criterion with no citable surface should not be assumed drivable. F1.26 is not a substitute: it is the sidecar that does NOT fit.
   - ADD A "FREE-FORM PASS" SUBSECTION to docs/visual-acceptance-checklist.md under "Recording a run", carrying item 3's capture list. That converts the owner's proposal from an argument he has to re-make each time into a recognised, recordable mode of Track B — which is what he actually wants, and it costs the release nothing.

ONE LINE FOR THE OWNER: yes, drive your own cubes — do it first, unprimed, and bring back a multi-GB promote run, because that is the one thing no agent and no fixture can get for us. But the F1 queue is not a to-do list the free-form pass can absorb; it is the evidence surface five done criteria point at, and two of them (DC2, DC13) are worded so that only ticking the rows can satisfy them.

py4dstemLens.refutation:
I attacked all three legs and could not break the verdict. What I ran and found:

ATTACK 1 — "the frame map P was fitted, not derived." If the py4DSTEM cross-check only works because someone hand-picked P = [[0,1,0],[1,0,0],[0,0,-1]], then a mutant plus a *different* proper map might score just as well, and leg 3 would prove nothing. I searched the ENTIRE space of 24 proper signed-permutation frame maps (not just the one map), scoring median symmetry-reduced misorientation over the prior agent's 40 py4DSTEM cases (/tmp/acomprobe/py4-truth.npy, /tmp/acomprobe/py4-out-*.json). CONFIRMED, I ran it:
- SHIPPING: best map is exactly the claimed lab_swap at median 2.06 deg (62% under 5 deg); second-best map 22.72 deg. The map is selected by a factor of 11, so it is not absorbing the answer.
- MUT-A: best-of-24 median 20.46 deg (map diag(-1,1,-1)); MUT-B: best-of-24 median 20.46 deg. No proper frame relabelling rescues either mutant. The prior agent's "det = -1, cannot be a frame relabelling" argument is therefore not just asserted — it is measured over the whole map space. This STRENGTHENS the verdict beyond what was claimed.
I also rebuilt the shipping harness myself from the repo tree and re-ran /tmp/acomprobe/py4-input.json: mean score 0.799, median 2.06 deg, best map = lab_swap — byte-reproducing /tmp/acomprobe/py4-out-base.json. The claim reproduces.

ATTACK 2 — "mutants A and B are strawmen." Both break internal template-vs-experimental consistency, so of course they fail; that does not show the SHARED convention is right. The failure mode that survives such a test is a GLOBAL mirror — mirror the template azimuth AND the experimental azimuth together. That is precisely the handedness class the derivation leans on crystal_viz.py to exclude, and the prior agent never mutated it. I built it (MUT-C: OrientationPlan.swift:194 atan2(-y,x) AND OrientationMatcher.swift:242 atan2(-dy,dx), /tmp/mutC, tracked tree untouched) and MUT-D (OrientationMatcher.swift:313-314 negation removed, /tmp/mutD). CONFIRMED, I ran both through the same 40 py4DSTEM patterns:
- MUT-C: mean score 0.799 (IDENTICAL to shipping), best-of-24 median 26.02 deg.
- MUT-D: mean score 0.799 (IDENTICAL), best-of-24 median 26.02 deg.
Both are caught decisively by leg 3 and both are invisible to the score. My hypothesis that cubic mirror symmetry might make a global mirror unobservable was wrong: the mirror is about a detector axis, not a crystal plane, so it is not absorbed by m-3m. The handedness anchor holds under direct experiment, not just by citation.

ATTACK 3 — citation audit at References/py4DSTEM-dev. Every cited line says what is claimed. crystal_ACOM.py:702-712 — I ran m1z@m2x@m3z in numpy and got R[:,2] = [0.30058672 0.50097786 0.81158414] = v exactly, det = 0.9999999999999997. Note the oddity the prior agent did not flag: crystal_ACOM.py:619 is azim = arctan2(vecs[:,0], vecs[:,1]) — arctan2(x, y), not the commented-out arctan2(y, x) at :616-618 — but the identity still holds, so the conclusion survives. crystal_viz.py:1009-1011 ax.scatter(qy, qx) plus :1072 ax.invert_yaxis() confirms qx = row (down), qy = column (right). crystal_ACOM.py:1542-1546 m3z rows [[c,s,0],[-s,c,0],[0,0,1]] on the right is byte-identical to OrientationResult.swift:101-104 columns (c,-s,0),(s,c,0),(0,0,1). crystal.py:855-856 gx_proj = g_diff[0], gy_proj = g_diff[1] confirms qx/qy are lab x/y.

ATTACK 4 — leg 3's truth matrices. py4gen.py builds truth with cry.parse_orientation(zone_axis_cartesian, proj_x_cartesian). The prior agent never checked what that returns. I did: crystal.py:1344-1350 — proj_y = cross(proj_z, proj_x), return np.vstack((proj_x, proj_y, proj_z)).T, i.e. lab axes in COLUMNS with column 2 = zone axis, and x cross y = z (right-handed). This is the convention the comparison assumes, so the truth matrices are sound. This was a real gap in the evidence chain and it closes clean.

ONE CAVEAT I WILL REGISTER AGAINST LEG 2, though it does not change the verdict. The claim that the analytic probe "does not call project()" is true — I read /tmp/acomprobe/main.swift:100-110, which places peaks at x = ox + g·f1/scale, y = oy + g·f2/scale from a basis built in the probe. But the probe's ground truth is mTrue = columns (f1, f2, n), i.e. the probe ASSERTS the very convention under test and then checks the app agrees with it. It is therefore a consistency test of project() vs the matcher vs ACOMOrientation.matrix against an assumed convention — not independent evidence that the convention matches the world. It is not circular in the code sense (no shared function), but it is convention-assuming, and the summary oversells it as one of three "independent lines." Only leg 3 is externally grounded. Leg 3 is strong enough to carry the verdict on its own, and I verified it independently, so the conclusion stands.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED on every line I tried. I redid the derivation from scratch without reading the other agent's algebra as authority, and built my own fixture. Both confirm the verdict.

MY DERIVATION (CONFIRMED by hand, then checked numerically).

(1) Basis handedness. `ACOMOrientation.detectorBasis` (Core/Analysis/OrientationResult.swift:91-95) sets e1 = normalize(n x ref), e2 = n x e1. Then e1 x e2 = e1 x (n x e1) = n(e1.e1) - e1(e1.n) = n, since e1 is perpendicular to n and unit. So (e1,e2,n) is orthonormal right-handed and det = +1 whenever |n| = 1. Zone axes are unit (Fibonacci-sphere sampling, OrientationResult.swift:182-188 and :440-446), and `bases = axes.map(ACOMOrientation.detectorBasis)` (OrientationPlan.swift:107) uses the SAME array the templates are projected from (:118), so no basis/template mismatch is possible. A left-handed basis here would silently produce det = -1 matrices; it does not — I measured det = 1.0000 on all 18 harness outputs.

(2) The composition. Let the pattern be the template rotated by theta: phi_exp = phi_tmpl + theta. Write g_perp = a*e1 + b*e2, a = rho*cos(phi), b = rho*sin(phi). Requiring g.E1 = rho*cos(phi+theta) = a*cos(theta) - b*sin(theta) forces E1 = e1*cos(theta) - e2*sin(theta); requiring g.E2 = rho*sin(phi+theta) forces E2 = e1*sin(theta) + e2*cos(theta). Stacking (E1, E2, n) as columns is exactly basis * inPlane with inPlane columns (c,-s,0),(s,c,0),(0,0,1) — precisely OrientationResult.swift:99-105. So `angle` MUST equal +theta = phi_exp - phi_tmpl. Sanity check at theta = 90 deg: E1 = -e2, E2 = e1, and a reflection at g = e1 reports atan2(g.E2, g.E1) = atan2(1,0) = 90 deg. Correct.

(3) The correlation sign, derived independently of FFT convention. vDSP_zvmul(..., -1) conjugates the FIRST factor, which is `experimental` (OrientationMatcher.swift:165-168). With forward X[k] = sum_a x[a] exp(-2pi i k a/N), conj(E)*T inverse-transformed gives corr[m] = sum_a E[a]*T[a+m]. With E[a] = T[a - m_theta], the argmax is m = -m_theta. Note this result is INVARIANT to which exponential sign the forward transform uses, provided the inverse is its opposite: with forward exp(+i) the two conjugations swap and the delta lands identically. So the negation `bin = (N - bestBin) % N` (OrientationMatcher.swift:313-314) yields +m_theta, i.e. angle = +theta — exactly what (2) requires. The negation is CORRECT, and correct for both outputs, because `angle` is the single value fed to BOTH the reported `inPlaneAngle` and `ACOMOrientation.matrix` (OrientationMatcher.swift:315-318). There is no second site to get out of step.

(4) The y-down question, which is where I expected to break it. The app never applies a y-flip, and it does not need one: it does not inherit a maths-convention (y-up) frame anywhere. It asserts x = column, y = row (Core/Analysis/DiskDetection.swift:34; the maxima loop indexes i = y*px + x at :634-639) and then requires (column, row, n) right-handed, which forces n = whatever makes that true. The physical anchor is py4DSTEM, and the other agent anchored it on PLOTTING (crystal_viz invert_yaxis) — a weak, easy-to-invert argument. There is a much harder anchor in array indexing that they missed: References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/preprocess/utils.py:191-195 — `maxima_x, maxima_y = np.nonzero(maxima_bool)` and `maxima["intensity"] = ar[maxima_x, maxima_y]`. numpy's nonzero returns axis 0 first, so py4DSTEM's "x"/qx is the ROW and qy is the COLUMN, with no plotting involved. Since py4DSTEM's orientation matrices are proper rotations whose column 2 is the zone axis (I verified numerically: for v = [0.30058672, 0.50097786, 0.81158414], column 2 of m1z@m2x@m3z from crystal_ACOM.py:691-712 equals v exactly, det = 0.9999999999999997), and k0 = [0,0,-1/lambda] at crystal_ACOM.py:716 puts the beam along -z_lab, py4DSTEM asserts row x column = UPSTREAM. The app asserts column x row = n. The two are the same physical statement iff n = downstream. No y-flip is needed or missing in either.

(5) The independent pin on n, which is the part that makes this "correct" and not merely "self-consistent". I re-derived the excitation error from |g + sg*n_f + k0| = |k0| with k0 = -K*zhat and foil normal n_f = -zhat: |g_perp|^2 + (g_z - sg)^2 - 2K(g_z - sg) = 0, so sg = g_z - (lambda/2)|g_perp|^2. That reproduces py4DSTEM's exact formula (2*g[2] - lambda*|g|^2)/(2 - 2*lambda*g[2]) at References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/process/diffraction/crystal.py:1368-1370 term for term, which validates my derivation apparatus against the reference. The app writes sg = g.n + (lambda/2)|g|^2 (OrientationPlan.swift:186). Under the frame map this equals MINUS py4DSTEM's sg — a pure sign flip, harmless because the weight is exp(-(sg/w)^2) and the cutoff is abs(sg) — but ONLY if n = -z_py = downstream. If n were upstream, g.n = -g_z would give sg = -g_z + (lambda/2)|g|^2 against a true -g_z - (lambda/2)|g|^2: the CURVATURE TERM's relative sign flips, which is not an overall sign and is different physics (it would excite -g where py4DSTEM excites +g, breaking the pi-degeneracy the wrong way).
